{{nihongo|'''Takinami Shrine'''|瀧浪神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kaga Province]].

'''Takinami Shrine''' (たきなみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Ōno-machi, {{ill|Komatsu, Ishikawa|Q646898|qid=Q646898}}, {{ill|Ishikawa Prefecture|Q131281|qid=Q131281}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takirihime no Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}} - Originally the enshrined deity of Kasanui Shrine, which was merged into this shrine.

=== History ===
The shrine is listed as Takinami Shrine (多伎奈弥神社) in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, and is also known as Takimiya. In the 11th year of {{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} ({{ill|AD 911|Q24062|qid=Q24062}}) under {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}, it was conferred the rank of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}}<ref name="jinjacho">[https://www.ishikawa-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/j0561/ Takinami Shrine] - Ishikawa Prefecture Shrine Agency</ref>.

In the 16th year of {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} ({{ill|1639|Q6897|qid=Q6897}}), when Lord {{ill|Maeda Toshitsune|Q587204|qid=Q587204}} retired to {{ill|Komatsu Castle|Q11461063|qid=Q11461063}}, he deeply revered this shrine and erected a worship hall.

On December 29, {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 39 ({{ill|1906|Q2049|qid=Q2049}}), the shrine was designated as a shinsen heihakuryō kyōshin shrine. On March 13, {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 41 ({{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}), Kasanui Shrine (Hashizume-tani lot 6) was merged into this shrine. Because the shrine was originally located on a mountaintop and therefore inconvenient for worship, on November 28, {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 17 ({{ill|1942|Q18625|qid=Q18625}}), the main hall, offering hall, and worship hall were rebuilt at the current shrine grounds<ref name="genbu">[https://www.genbu.net/data/kaga/takinami_title.htm Takinami Shrine] - Genbu</ref>.
